This foundational step enables the formulation of Tchebycheff’s inequality by establishing a link between mean convergence and measure-theoretic convergence. Kolmogoroff’s inequality emerges as a limiting case of Tchebycheff’s when applied to single-step variance bounds. The interplay between these results reveals how probabilistic inequalities can be used to infer convergence properties in functional analysis. Failure modes arise when assumptions about boundedness or finite variance are violated, leading to breakdowns in both convergence and inequality validity.
